subject: Order form: IP infringement liability carve-out — proposed allocation and royalty offset
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Order form: IP infringement liability carve-out — proposed allocation and royalty offset

Liam / Novum team,

Thanks again for the productive call this morning. Per Erin's ask, we circulated the initial order form with a liability cap carve-out tied to IP indemnity. Novum asked for clarity on exposure allocation and whether we can accept a full carve-out (i.e., remove the monetary cap for IP claims).

Quick summary of what we'd like to propose as a starting point (attached as redline):
- IP indemnity remains: Redwood will indemnify for third-party claims alleging direct infringement of Novum's specific use of the Services.
- Carve-out mechanics: rather than an unlimited removal of the monetary cap, we propose a targeted enhanced-cap model for IP-only indemnity equal to 2x the customer's trailing 12-month Redwood spend, subject to a maximum of $5,000,000.
- Royalty-offset option: if a claim results in a royalty or recurring payment, Redwood's payment obligations will net any royalties already paid by Novum to the third party (i.e., credits for pre-existing royalties), and Redwood may offset future recurring fees against amounts owed under an IP judgment, subject to audit rights.
- Escrow alternative: for customers that want further comfort, we can agree to an escrow equal to 6 months of committed fees (or a negotiated multiple) that Redwood funds within 30 days after claim acceptance.
- Defense and settlement: Redwood requests lead defense/control with Novum approval for settlements that would impose non-financial obligations on Redwood or admissions of liability.

Please see the attached redline for clause-level text. If this model looks directionally acceptable, Marissa (cc'd) and I will work to tighten the wording to make it procurement-friendly.

Thanks,
Ben

Subject: Re: Order form: IP infringement liability carve-out — proposed allocation and royalty offset

Ben — thanks for the note and the redline. High-level feedback from our GC and procurement:
- We appreciate a capped enhancement vs. a full unlimited carve-out. Novum would prefer removal of the cap for IP only where the infringement claim is tied to our specific data or custom model artifacts we provide (i.e., not for general model weights).
- Royalty offset sounds reasonable but must not allow Redwood to avoid paying amounts already awarded by a court. Offsets should be limited to documented, contractual royalty payments to a third party that Novum actually made prior to the judgment.
- Escrow is interesting; procurement wants clarity on how funds are posted, what triggers release, and whether posting the escrow is a condition precedent to start of the contract term.
- Settlement control: Novum insists on joint control for any settlement that would bind Novum or require ongoing payments.

Can your legal team give a clean clause we can exchange with our counsel? Also: procurement asked whether Redwood would consider a short-term separate insurance top-up in addition to the escrow (e.g., policy endorsement for IP claims).

--
Liam

Liam — appreciate the quick read-through. Below is proposed clause language that addresses Novum's points while limiting ambiguity. This is intended for insertion into the Order Form/Exhibit A.

--- Proposed Order Form Language (draft) ---
"IP Indemnity and Enhanced Cap for IP Claims. Redwood shall indemnify, defend and hold harmless Customer from and against any third-party claim alleging that Customer's specific use of the Services, including Customer-provided data, custom prompts, or Customer-uploaded model artifacts, directly infringes a third party's issued patent, copyright or registered work ("IP Claim"). For IP Claims only, the monetary limitation of liability set forth in the Agreement shall be increased to the greater of: (i) two times the Customer's aggregate paid Redwood fees during the twelve (12) months preceding the claim, and (ii) $100,000, up to a maximum of $5,000,000 (the "Enhanced IP Cap"). Amounts paid under this Section shall be reduced by any documented royalty payments actually made by Customer to the third party prior to final judgment.

Defense and Settlement. Redwood shall have the right to assume defense of any IP Claim with counsel of its choice; provided, however, that Redwood shall not enter into any settlement that (a) admits fault on behalf of Customer, (b) requires Customer to take or refrain from taking any action in its business, or (c) obligates Customer to make any payment, without Customer's prior written consent (which shall not be unreasonably withheld). If Redwood assumes defense, Customer shall reasonably cooperate with Redwood and may participate in the defense at its own expense.

Escrow and Insurance Option. As an alternative to removing the cap entirely, Redwood agrees to: (a) deposit into an independent escrow account an amount equal to six (6) months of Customer's committed fees under the Order Form within thirty (30) days of signature; and/or (b) procure an IP coverage endorsement to Redwood's liability insurance policy covering third-party IP claims up to an agreed upon limit. Release of escrow shall follow final resolution or agreement among the parties and escrow agent; subject to an accounting for any amounts previously paid to Customer under this Section.

Audit and Offsets. Any offsets for royalties shall be subject to Customer providing reasonable supporting documentation; Redwood may audit such documentation with advance notice and under NDA. Offsets shall not apply to amounts awarded by a final court judgment that reflect damages for which Customer already received royalties from a third party.

--- end draft ---

Open items for us to agree with Novum:
1) Whether the Enhanced IP Cap should be fixed at 2x trailing 12 months or tied to committed annual spend in the Order Form.
2) Exact escrow mechanics (who funds, timing, and whether escrow is a condition precedent).
3) Insurance endorsement feasibility and cost — Karthik, can infra/finance model a premium impact?

Ben — can you confirm whether procurement would accept an escrow that posts within 30 days post-signature vs. being a condition precedent? Liam, if you can share Novum's procurement playbook language on escrow triggers that would help.

Regards,
Marissa

Team — quick operational notes from pricing/finance:
- Escrow funding: modeling shows Redwood can post 6 months' escrow for customers with ACV >= $500k without materially impacting cash runway; smaller deals we'd want the escrow to be funded by Novum or via a premium on price.
- Enhanced cap approach tied to "committed fees" in the Order Form is cleaner for sales and predictable for finance. Trailing-12 calculation can be disputed if there were one-off credits; recommend "committed fees in the Order Form" as the denominator.
- Insurance endorsements: add ~0.1% - 0.3% premium on top of our current liability program depending on the limit — we need underwriter confirmation.

I'll loop finance to get exact premium numbers if we go that route.

Karthik

Marissa / Ben — helpful draft. A couple of clarifying questions from our side:
1) The "documented royalty payments" carve-out — would Novum be required to show executed invoices/agreements? We want to avoid an open-ended accounting dispute.
2) If Redwood assumes defense and settles without Novum's written consent (in breach of the clause), would Redwood then be liable for the full award even if previously limited by the Enhanced IP Cap?
3) Can the escrow release mechanics include a short interim release for defense costs (reasonable counsel fees) subject to escrow agent approval and a cap?

Also, procurement prefers that the escrow be posted by Redwood within 30 days of signature, not as a condition precedent. That aligns with implementation schedules.

--
Liam

Liam / Erin / procurement — great points. Quick responses and next steps: 
- Documentation for royalty offsets: yes, Novum would need to provide executed agreements/invoices. Marissa's draft already calls for "reasonable supporting documentation"; we'll add a short list of acceptable docs (signed license, court-ordered payment schedule, bank remittance copies). Redwood reserves the right to audit those documents with reasonable notice and under NDA.
- Settlement control breach: Marissa confirms that if Redwood settles in breach of the consent requirement, Redwood would remain liable for amounts caused by such settlement and could not invoke the Enhanced IP Cap to escape liability for those amounts. We'll add explicit language.
- Interim escrow releases: acceptable for defense costs up to a negotiated threshold (suggest $250k or 25% of escrow, whichever is lower) with releases via the escrow agent upon submission of invoices and escrow agent approval.

Action items:
1) Marissa to circulate a second-pass redline (clause edits above + sample acceptable docs list) by EOD tomorrow.
2) Karthik to get ballpark insurance premium from underwriter and confirm whether endorsement is feasible.
3) Liam / Novum: confirm whether the Enhanced IP Cap formula should use "Committed Fees" or "Trailing 12 months paid fees".

If we can lock these three items this week, I can get procurement legal to push to signature next week. Thanks all.

Ben
